calls.head: Where the Maple Leafs have the edge: the power play
calls.body: The Maple Leafs are near the top of the league for the power play, and the Blackhawks are the worst. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one.
calls.call: The Maple Leafs’ power play creates more per 60 than the Blackhawks’.

calls.body: The Blackhawks are around the middle of the league for depth, and the Maple Leafs are one of the worst. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one.

surprises.head: Toronto brought the hits
surprises.body: Toronto usually hits less than most teams. Not tonight: a hit score of 195 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 87 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 225 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

surprises.head: A rough night for Sergei Bobrovsky
surprises.body: Bobrovsky allowed 6 goals on 25 shots, worth 3.2 expected goals: 2.8 more than expected. Starting goalies have a night this rough about once every 25 starts.

story.head: The Blackhawks pour it on late
paras: Easton Cowan struck first for the Maple Leafs early in the first. It was a busy second period. Frank Nazar tied it up for Chicago on the power play midway through the period, and he struck again less than five minutes later to put the Blackhawks ahead 2-1. Teddy Blueger tied it 2-2 for Toronto 22 seconds later. Connor Bedard put the Blackhawks back ahead 3-2, 35 seconds later. The third period was a wild one. Bedard left early in the period and didn’t return. The next day, he was listed as day to day with a shoulder injury. Tyler Bertuzzi made it 4-2 for the Blackhawks on the power play midway through the period, but John Tavares cut Chicago’s lead to 4-3 just over two minutes later. Oliver Moore and Bertuzzi scored 49 seconds apart later in the period to push the lead to 6-3, and the Leafs had no answer. Two players had three-point nights: Sam Rinzel with three assists, and Bertuzzi with two goals and an assist.

The chances were closer than the score. Spencer Knight made 31 saves for the Blackhawks, and Sergei Bobrovsky allowed six goals on 25 shots. The Blackhawks improved to 6-13-2, still last in the Central, while the Maple Leafs fell to 8-13-2, still last in the Atlantic.
